blocks.text: Imagine trying to predict an election result by asking only your friends. How reliable would your prediction be?

blocks.markdown: In data analysis, sampling is a crucial step that can significantly impact the conclusions drawn from data. This lesson explores different sampling methods and the biases that can arise if sampling is not done correctly.

blocks.title: Sampling
blocks.text: Sampling is the process of selecting a subset of individuals from a population to estimate characteristics of the whole population.

blocks.markdown: The goal of sampling is to obtain a representative subset of the population. This allows us to make inferences about the population without examining every individual.

blocks.title: Random Sampling
blocks.text: Random sampling is a method where each member of the population has an equal chance of being selected.

blocks.markdown: Random sampling is often considered the gold standard because it minimizes bias and ensures the sample is representative of the population.

blocks.title: Stratified Sampling
blocks.text: Stratified sampling involves dividing the population into subgroups (strata) and randomly sampling from each stratum.

blocks.markdown: Stratified sampling ensures that specific subgroups are adequately represented in the sample, which can be particularly important when certain subgroups are small but important.

blocks.title: Convenience Sampling
blocks.text: Convenience sampling involves selecting samples that are easiest to access, rather than those that are most representative.

blocks.markdown: While convenience sampling is easy and cost-effective, it often leads to biased results because it does not represent the entire population accurately.

blocks.title: Example of Random Sampling
blocks.prompt: A researcher wants to study the average height of students in a university. Describe how they might use random sampling.

steps.text: List all students in the university, assigning each a unique number.
Use a random number generator to select a subset of students.
Collect height data from the selected students.

blocks.answer: By using a random number generator, each student has an equal chance of being selected, minimizing bias.

blocks.title: Example of Stratified Sampling
blocks.prompt: A company wants to survey employee satisfaction across different departments. How might they use stratified sampling?

steps.text: Divide employees into strata based on department.
Randomly select a proportional number of employees from each department.
Conduct the survey with the selected employees.

blocks.answer: Stratified sampling ensures each department is represented proportionally, providing a more comprehensive view of employee satisfaction.

blocks.title: Impact of Sample Size
blocks.text: Larger sample sizes generally lead to more precise estimates of population parameters, reducing the margin of error.

blocks.markdown: Sample size plays a critical role in the precision of statistical estimates. Larger samples tend to yield more reliable results, but they also require more resources to collect and analyze.

points: Random sampling minimizes bias by giving each individual an equal chance of selection.
Stratified sampling ensures representation of specific subgroups within the population.
Convenience sampling is prone to bias and should be used cautiously.
